Recommended solution guide; original case outcome not confirmed:

Troubleshooting guide — recommended procedure

1. Read the exact model/product number and photograph the initial firmware screen if it lists a Boot Menu or Setup key.

2. If Windows starts in UEFI mode, open Advanced startup and choose Troubleshoot → Advanced options → UEFI Firmware Settings when offered.

3. Connect a known-good USB before restarting. In firmware, select its one-time boot/override entry if available.

4. If Windows does not start and the screen gives no key, obtain the exact model manual or manufacturer support instruction. Do not assume a guessed universal Haier key is verified.
